incident.date: 5 de julho de 2024 — Voo LA8159 — Aeroporto SCL (ver Fatos Fixos do Incidente)

incident_timestamp_display: 5 de julho de 2024 — Voo LA8159 — Aeroporto SCL (ver Fatos Fixos do Incidente)
allegation_summary: It is alleged that DGAC (Direccion General de Aeronautica Civil) officials present at the airport during the LA8159 incident failed to exercise their regulatory oversight authority. Despite (1) a DGAC official confirming the passenger was right after PDI CCTV review (STG-7), (2) witnessing the passenger's forcible removal without documentation, and (3) being the regulatory body responsible for enforcing CACH Art. 133, DGAC took no enforcement action, issued no citations, and allowed LATAM to proceed with the document fabrication scheme and lifetime ban without intervention. This failure to exercise regulatory authority enabled LATAM's systematic procedural violations.

articles.article_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 133 — Denegacion de Embarque
articles.article_text:
1. A eleccion del pasajero:

a) Embarcar en el siguiente vuelo que tenga disponible el transportador, o en un transporte alternativo, si es que decidiera persistir en el contrato de transporte aereo.  
b) El reembolso del monto total pagado por el billete, si el pasajero se desiste del contrato de transporte aereo y este no hubiera comenzado su ejecucion.
articles.applicability_rationale: DGAC is the regulatory body responsible for enforcing CACH, including Art. 133. The agency's failure to intervene despite witnessing violations and confirming the carrier's allegations were false constitutes an abdication of its statutory oversight mandate. | legacy paraphrase: El transportador podra denegar el embarque... para lo cual debera: 1.- A eleccion del pasajero... 2.- El transportador debera ofrecer una compensacion...

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 184 — Atribuciones de la DGAC
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.184 from bcn.cl/leychile (DFL 221 de 1931 / Ley 18.916)
Confirm whether Art. 184 establishes DGAC's general supervisory and enforcement powers over air transport operations
Verify that the article imposes affirmative duties (not merely discretionary powers) on DGAC to intervene when carrier conduct violates the Code
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 184 likely defines DGAC's institutional mandate to supervise compliance with the Codigo Aeronautico. If it establishes mandatory oversight duties, DGAC's explicit disclaimer ('esta decision no la decidimos nosotros') while witnessing confirmed-false allegations against a passenger would constitute a breach of its statutory function.
candidate_articles.history_note: Proposed as the organic-authority article that grounds the 'abdication of oversight' theory. Not previously cited in the bundle.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 2 — Autoridad Aeronautica
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.2 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 2 designates DGAC as the authority responsible for applying and enforcing the Code
Determine if the article creates a non-delegable duty or merely an institutional designation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 2 likely establishes DGAC as the competent authority for enforcement of the entire Codigo Aeronautico. Combined with the factual record showing DGAC deferred entirely to the carrier's narrative and disclaimed decision-making authority, this article would ground the argument that DGAC cannot lawfully abdicate its role to a private party.
candidate_articles.history_note: Foundational article defining DGAC's institutional role. Not in the established bundle.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 134 — Obligaciones del Transportador en caso de cancelacion o retraso
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.134 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether Art. 134 extends passenger-protection obligations to situations where the carrier causes a passenger to miss a flight through wrongful denial of boarding
Assess whether DGAC has a supervisory duty to ensure compliance with Art. 134 remedies
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If Art. 134 imposes carrier obligations when a passenger loses their flight due to carrier action, DGAC's failure to enforce those obligations in real time (despite being physically present and aware the allegations were false) reinforces the abdication theory.
candidate_articles.history_note: Adjacent to established Art. 133; likely contains complementary duties. Not yet verified.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 150 — Responsabilidad del Transportador
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.150 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 150 establishes carrier liability for damages caused by wrongful denial of transport
Assess whether DGAC has enforcement or adjudicatory duties under this provision
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 150 likely establishes the carrier's civil liability framework. DGAC's regulatory role would include ensuring carriers do not escape liability by fabricating justifications for denial of boarding. The agency's passive acceptance of the carrier's narrative despite CCTV evidence to the contrary may constitute a failure to protect the passenger's rights under this provision.
candidate_articles.history_note: Proposed to establish the liability framework that DGAC should have been enforcing. Exact article number requires verification — CACH liability provisions may be in a different article.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Constitucion Politica de la Republica, Art. 19 Nr. 3 — Igual proteccion de la ley en el ejercicio de sus derechos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CPR Art. 19 Nr. 3 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that the guarantee of equal protection and due process applies to administrative proceedings and state-agent interactions with individuals
Assess whether DGAC's uncritical adoption of the carrier's version without independent verification violates procedural fairness guarantees
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 19 Nr. 3 guarantees equal protection and due process. DGAC's conduct — accepting the carrier's allegations at face value, refusing to exercise independent judgment, and telling the passenger to seek legal remedies on his own — may violate the constitutional guarantee that state organs must afford individuals fair treatment when exercising authority that affects their rights.
candidate_articles.history_note: Constitutional due-process provision. Relevant because DGAC is a state organ exercising public authority at the moment of the incident.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Constitucion Politica de la Republica, Art. 19 Nr. 22 — No discriminacion arbitraria en el trato del Estado en materia economica
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CPR Art. 19 Nr. 22 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether the prohibition of arbitrary discrimination by the State in economic matters extends to regulatory agencies favoring a carrier over a consumer
Assess applicability to DGAC's conduct of deferring entirely to LATAM's narrative
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 19 Nr. 22 prohibits arbitrary discrimination by the State in economic matters. DGAC's systematic deference to the carrier's version — while disclaiming any duty to the passenger — could constitute arbitrary favoritism toward the regulated entity at the expense of the consumer.
candidate_articles.history_note: Constitutional economic-equality provision. Proposed as supplementary constitutional ground.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley 19.496 (Ley de Proteccion al Consumidor), Art. 3 letra b — Derecho a informacion veraz y oportuna
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Ley 19.496 Art. 3 letra b from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether the consumer's right to truthful information creates a correlative duty on regulatory agencies to not propagate or endorse false carrier narratives
Assess whether DGAC's repetition of the carrier's unverified allegations to the passenger violates this consumer right
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 3 letra b guarantees consumers the right to truthful and timely information. While the primary duty-bearer is the provider, DGAC's role in relaying and endorsing the carrier's false narrative to the passenger — without independent verification — may constitute state complicity in violating this consumer right.
candidate_articles.history_note: Consumer-protection provision. Proposed to bridge the regulatory-failure theory with consumer-rights framework.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 186 — Facultades fiscalizadoras de la DGAC
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CACH.Art.186 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 186 grants DGAC specific inspection and enforcement powers over carrier compliance with passenger rights
Verify the exact article number — CACH enforcement powers may be in Art. 184, 185, or 186
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If Art. 186 grants DGAC specific enforcement and inspection powers, the agency's failure to exercise those powers when confronted with evidence that the carrier's allegations were false would constitute a dereliction of statutory duty. The exact article number within the CACH enforcement chapter requires verification.
candidate_articles.history_note: Proposed as the specific enforcement-powers article. Exact numbering uncertain — verification needed against the actual CACH text.
